slides.text: Before a soul is permitted into heaven, it must walk through the Archive of Forked Roads. Every shelf holds the leather-bound volumes of the lives you almost lived—the cities you didn't move to, the battles you fled, the hands you were too shy to hold. Most men weep for centuries in those aisles, reading about the kings and heroes they might have been.

When Tomas, a village cobbler who had spent eighty years mending boots in a leaky cottage, entered his personal alcove, the Archivist took pity on him. 'Here,' the angel said softly, pointing to a towering tome bound in gold leaf and dragon-scale. 'In this volume, you took the Duke's commission at nineteen. You conquered three continents and died on a diamond throne.'

Tomas ran his calloused thumb over the golden spine, then left it unopened and reached instead for a worn, dog-eared booklet at the end of the shelf—the record of the quiet life he had actually lived. 'Does the golden book have the rainy Tuesday when my wife burnt the plum tarts and we danced in the kitchen smoke?' he asked. The angel shook his head. Tomas smiled. 'Then I chose the richest one.'
